questions.q: What is consistent about NULL comparison across SQL Server, Oracle, MySQL, and PostgreSQL?
options: = NULL never matches anywhere -- you must use IS NULL / IS NOT NULL on every platform
Only Oracle requires IS NULL; the others allow = NULL
= NULL works correctly on all platforms except PostgreSQL
NULL comparison behavior is actually the most inconsistent part of SQL across these platforms
questions.explain: This is the one NULL-related behavior that's genuinely portable across all four platforms in this course.

questions.q: What is Oracle's famous, documented quirk regarding empty strings in VARCHAR2 columns?
options: Oracle treats an empty string ('') as NULL
Oracle rejects empty strings with an error at insert time
Oracle stores empty strings as a single space character automatically
Oracle treats NULL as an empty string, the reverse of the real behavior
questions.explain: Oracle's well-documented quirk is that '' is treated as NULL when stored in a VARCHAR2 column.

questions.q: On SQL Server, MySQL, and PostgreSQL, if you insert an empty string into a column and then run WHERE column = '', what happens?
options: It matches the row, because '' and NULL are distinct values on these platforms
It never matches anything, the same as on Oracle
It throws an error because empty strings are not allowed
It matches every row in the table regardless of value
questions.explain: Unlike Oracle, these platforms treat '' and NULL as genuinely distinct, so an equality check against '' correctly matches.

questions.q: Why does Oracle's empty-string behavior catch developers off guard specifically?
options: Code distinguishing 'no value given' (NULL) from 'a blank value was given' ('') silently loses that distinction with no error when run against Oracle
Oracle throws a loud, obvious error the moment an empty string is inserted
It only affects numeric columns, not string columns
It happens identically on every platform, so there's nothing unusual about it
questions.explain: The failure is silent -- no error occurs, the empty string just becomes NULL, which can break logic that relied on telling them apart.

questions.q: What does Chapter 3 move on to covering after this NULL/empty-string lesson closes out Chapter 2?
options: Querying basics across dialects, including pagination, string concatenation, identifier quoting, and case sensitivity
An entirely new course on database administration
A repeat of Chapter 1's platform introductions
Only PL/SQL procedural code, skipping all other platforms
questions.explain: Chapter 3, 'Querying Basics Compared,' picks up pagination, concatenation, quoting, case sensitivity, and more, in greater depth.
